lines.text: At dawn, the Measurers brought a covered cart into the square, for the children.
Magister. These six are my wards, members of my household. Under the Eleventh Article and the Fourth, you can't take them without a royal warrant.
No. It doesn't. Unload the cart.
I don't think Greyhollow had ever made that much noise.
Do you know why the Order exists? Three hundred years ago, there was a woman in the north. Hollow-born, like you. Everything she touched grew. Her people loved her.
And when she died, the whole North froze. The Pale is her grave, my lord. That is what your kind leaves behind.
I knelt in your barley last night. The soil is warm a foot deep. I know exactly what you are.
So here is my offer. Come south with me, quietly. The Order will take care of you. And Greyhollow will be left in peace. Your people keep their barley. Their children. Everything.
I looked back at the village. At Bram by the gate. At six children being squeezed half to death by their mothers.
I thought you would say that. Then the warrant will come, my lord. And it will come with soldiers.
He walked back into the mist. I stood in the warm barley for a long time. For the first time in my life, I wished I really was nothing at all.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter 26, coming soon.
